questions.question: What is the Sun, and where is the Earth in the solar system?
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is a star: a huge, very hot ball of glowing gas that gives out its own heat and light. It is about 150 million kilometres away. Eight planets travel around the Sun, and the Earth is the third planet from the Sun. The Sun, the planets and their moons make up the solar system.

questions.question: What is an orbit, and what keeps the Earth in its orbit?
questions.expected_answer: An orbit is the path that something follows as it travels around another object in space. The Earth follows an orbit around the Sun that is almost a circle. The pull of the Sun's gravity keeps the Earth in its orbit, so it keeps curving around the Sun instead of flying off into space.

questions.question: Explain what a year is and why we have a leap year.
questions.expected_answer: A year is the time the Earth takes to travel once around the Sun, about 365 days. The trip really takes about 365 and a quarter days, so every four years the four extra quarters add up to one whole day. That day is added as 29 February, and that year, a leap year, has 366 days.
